scope: FK consistency, index coverage hot queries, UNIQUE coverage append-only tables, JSON column integrity, timestamp/date conventions
method: Read-only grep + targeted migration/model inspection. 169 migrations + 79 models + ~83 FK declarations + 33 UNIQUE constraints inventoried.

baseline_drift_from_f1.verdict: Drift is fully explained by Wave-G/H/Loyalty heals; no orphan migrations or undocumented models.

findings.title: audit_logs.branch_id has NO FK to branches.id
findings.impact: branch_id and user_id are integer-only references. NF525 audit_logs survives branch hard-delete (branches uses SoftDeletes so prod risk is theoretical), but the schema does not enforce that audit_logs.branch_id ever pointed to a real branch. Garbage writes from a buggy service layer (similar to the webhook_events.order_id case fixed in 2026_05_18_120000) would silently succeed.
findings.mitigation_present: AuditLogService is the sole authorised writer (per migration docblock POS-9.4.3) + immutability triggers prevent UPDATE/DELETE so bad rows are permanent.
findings.recommendation: Add nullable FK with nullOnDelete on audit_logs.branch_id and audit_logs.user_id, after scrub-pass like the webhook_events.order_id heal (2026_05_18_120000). Same pattern: NULL out orphan rows, then ADD CONSTRAINT. NF525-safe: nullOnDelete fires only on hard-delete and Branch hard-delete is prevented by SoftDeletes on the parent.

findings.title: z_reports.branch_id / opened_by / closed_by have NO FK
findings.impact: Same shape as DBA-001: integer-only columns. opened_by/closed_by reference users.id implicitly. A buggy ZReportService write could persist garbage user_id values; the immutability migration 2026_05_09_160000 then makes them undeletable. Hardens audit drift between Z report aggregates and User table.
findings.mitigation_present: ZReportService is sole writer; cache lock + UNIQUE(branch_id, sequence_no) prevent forks.
findings.recommendation: Same as DBA-001: nullable FK with nullOnDelete on branch_id, opened_by, closed_by.

findings.title: cash_movements.branch_id and cash_movements.order_id have NO FK
findings.impact: Fiscal-adjacent append-only table (delete-trigger added in 2026_05_16_130000) but no FK enforcement. order_id orphan rows possible if Order is soft-deleted then PRUNE is run later; branch_id orphan rows possible if a Branch is force-deleted bypassing SoftDeletes. Both scenarios are off-path today, but the foundation is weaker than the cash_drawer_session_id FK (which is cascadeOnDelete).
findings.mitigation_present: DELETE trigger (immutability) prevents row removal; service layer is sole writer.
findings.recommendation: Add nullable FK + nullOnDelete on order_id; non-nullable FK + restrictOnDelete on branch_id (consistent with stock_movements post 2026_05_18_140000 heal).

findings.title: pending_payment_confirmations.branch_id and order_id have NO FK
findings.impact: Reconciliation queue for TPE transactions — orphan order_id possible if Order is soft-deleted while a pending confirmation is still in-flight. UNIQUE(transaction_id) catches replay but not orphan parent.
findings.mitigation_present: UNIQUE(transaction_id) blocks replay; status enum + retry_count for reconciliation.
findings.recommendation: Add FK on order_id with restrictOnDelete (Order is SoftDelete, hard delete is forbidden anyway; FK would block force-delete attempts). Same for branch_id.

findings.title: FreshOrderSeed command TRUNCATEs orders + order_items with no environment guard
findings.impact: TRUNCATE bypasses MySQL triggers — so audit_logs DELETE trigger does NOT fire if cleanup ever extends to those tables. Currently scoped to orders/order_items only, but the pattern of SET FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0 + TRUNCATE is dangerous: order_payments cascadeOnDelete chain becomes moot, FKs lose enforcement, and audit_logs may end up pointing to dead orders. NO environment guard (`if (app()->environment('production')) throw`) — `php artisan seed:fresh-orders` against prod would wipe orders+order_items silently. Matches BRAIN deploy-doc TRUNCATE concern verbatim.
findings.mitigation_present: Production GRANT level (deploy doc owner-deferred) is the only mitigation, and BRAIN flags this as such.
findings.recommendation: Add environment guard at top of handle(): `if (app()->environment('production')) { throw new RuntimeException('seed:fresh-orders forbidden in production - TRUNCATE bypasses NF525 immutability triggers'); }`. Identical pattern to the audit_logs down() migration guard at line 70-76 of 2026_04_22_000002. Single-LOC heal, no schema change, P0 because the command is exposed via artisan.

findings.title: loyalty_transactions UNIQUE(user_id, order_id, type) — type='earn' multi-row possible across orders, single-redemption invariant only on (user, order)
findings.evidence_excerpt: UNIQUE(user_id, order_id, type) — covers "single redemption per order"
findings.impact: UNIQUE is correct for redemption (one redeem per order). For earn rows with order_id=NULL (manual_add via admin), NULL semantics on UNIQUE in MySQL/SQLite ≥3.9 allow multiple NULL order_id rows per (user, type). Acceptable per docblock, but a per-source_surface UNIQUE could tighten further (out of V1 scope).
findings.mitigation_present: Service layer (PosRedemptionService etc.) enforces single redemption; DB is defence-in-depth.
findings.recommendation: V1: accept. V1.0.2: consider partial UNIQUE WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL + a separate idempotency_key UNIQUE for kiosk/web/mobile redeem paths.

findings.title: JSON columns lack DB-level structural validation (composition_snapshot, allergens_snapshot, payload)
findings.evidence_excerpt: $table->json('composition_snapshot')->nullable();  // no CHECK constraint, no schema validation
findings.impact: Eloquent casts 'array' deserialise on read. If a column is corrupted at write-time (bad encoding, truncation, version skew), read-time defensive parsing in services like OrderDetailsResource or KdsItemResource silently returns NULL or partial data. composition_snapshot is the NF525 evidence of what the customer paid for — corruption here = fiscal evidence loss.
findings.mitigation_present: Writers (PricingService::calculateOrder) populate via json_encode of structured PHP arrays; Eloquent throws on malformed JSON read. No prod incident logged.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.2: MySQL 8.0+ supports JSON CHECK constraints. Add CHECK (JSON_VALID(composition_snapshot)) and CHECK (JSON_EXTRACT(composition_snapshot, '$.template_id') IS NOT NULL) for critical columns. SQLite needs application-layer JSON schema validator. Out of V1 scope, but document the gap.

findings.title: Missing composite index (branch_id, status, order_datetime) on orders for KDS/OSS hot queries
findings.evidence_excerpt: Existing indexes: idx_orders_branch_status (branch_id, status), idx_orders_datetime (order_datetime), idx_orders_status (status). MISSING: (branch_id, status, order_datetime) covering composite.
findings.impact: KDS hot list path uses three separate indexes — MySQL optimiser typically picks (branch_id, status) and filters on order_datetime via Index Range Scan + filesort. At Le Cayenne V1 single-resto scale (~200 orders/day), zero measurable impact. At V2 SaaS multi-branch scale (10k+/day per branch), p95 latency would degrade.
findings.mitigation_present: V1 traffic shape makes this a non-issue.
findings.recommendation: Defer to V1.0.2. Add `$table->index(['branch_id', 'status', 'order_datetime'], 'orders_kds_oss_hot_idx')` in a non-breaking additive migration when V2 SaaS scale is on the roadmap.

findings.title: source_surface column on orders is not indexed
findings.impact: FrontendOrderService:822 does `->where('source_surface', 'kiosk')` without an index. Single-resto V1 = irrelevant. Reporting/analytics path at scale = mild degradation.
findings.mitigation_present: Composite indexes idx_orders_branch_status pre-filter so source_surface scan happens on a tiny subset.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.2 deferred. Optional non-breaking additive index on (branch_id, source_surface, created_at).

findings.title: cash_movements has NO idempotency UNIQUE — append-only + retry-safe assumption broken
findings.evidence_line: 2026_05_08_140100 lines 28-51 (table definition, only id+FK+composite indexes, NO UNIQUE)
findings.impact: stock_movements has UNIQUE(idempotency_key) (DBA-001 confirms) — append-only with replay defence. cash_movements is ALSO append-only (DELETE trigger 2026_05_16_130000), but lacks idempotency UNIQUE. Scenario: cashier action retries (network blip, button double-click) cause 2 cash_movements rows for the same logical event. Immutability trigger then makes the duplicate PERMANENT. Cash reconciliation (X/Z report) reads cash_movements aggregate — duplicate row inflates the cash total, breaking NF525 fiscal closure invariants. Same shape applies to order_payments (no reference/transaction_id UNIQUE).
findings.mitigation_present: Service layer (CashDrawerService) likely uses Cache::lock + idempotency middleware to prevent double-submit. Not a code-side replay leak today.
findings.recommendation: Add nullable `idempotency_key` column + UNIQUE constraint on cash_movements (mirror stock_movements pattern). Same for order_payments. Migration is additive; backfill existing rows = NULL (legacy rows not idempotency-protected). New writes MUST populate. Symmetric inverse of DBA-006 (loyalty UNIQUE present, cash UNIQUE absent).

findings.title: order_payments lacks UNIQUE on reference field — multi-tender retry replay possible
findings.impact: If a TPE transaction's reference (card 4-last-digits + amount) is replayed (network retry), TWO rows insert. cashier sees 2x amount in receipt. No DB-level guard. Same class as DBA-011.
findings.mitigation_present: SplitPaymentService likely guards against this at service layer.
findings.recommendation: Add UNIQUE(order_id, mode, reference) WHERE reference IS NOT NULL (partial UNIQUE). MySQL 8.0+ supports functional indexes; SQLite supports partial indexes. Or use a deterministic idempotency_key column like stock_movements.

findings.title: JSON column read-time defensive parsing — Eloquent throws on malformed JSON, no fallback (read-time)
findings.evidence_excerpt: 'composition_snapshot' => 'array', // Eloquent json_decode; throws InvalidArgumentException on malformed JSON
findings.impact: Write-time integrity addressed by DBA-007 (no DB-level CHECK). Read-time: Eloquent json_decode in 'array' cast THROWS on malformed JSON. A corrupt row (manual UPDATE attempting unicode injection, ASCII NUL byte, truncation) crashes the model load. KDS list / receipt generation that fetches such an OrderItem will 500 — no graceful degradation. Combined with immutability triggers, recovery requires SQL surgery.
findings.mitigation_present: Writes via PricingService::calculateOrder use structured PHP arrays + json_encode — corruption requires raw SQL manipulation.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.2: add accessor on OrderItem for composition_snapshot with try/catch fallback to empty array + Log::warning. Defensive read-time pattern for fiscal-critical JSON. Mirror for AuditLog.payload, ZReport.total_by_method, domain_events.payload.

findings.title: fiscal_sequence_no = unsignedBigInteger (non-issue, documented for completeness)
findings.impact: 9.2 quintillion max — at 1M orders/day per branch = 25 billion years to overflow. Non-issue. Worth noting because the audit task asked about BIGINT overflow on long-running counters.

summary.next_class_of_finding: DBA-001..004 + DBA-011 + DBA-012 — append-only audit-adjacent tables consistently missing FK enforcement (audit_logs, z_reports, cash_movements, pending_payment_confirmations) OR missing idempotency UNIQUE (cash_movements, order_payments). Defence-in-depth gap; not a blocker because service layer + immutability triggers cover the gap, but a forensic-grade DB schema would constrain them.
